He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball|Florida Gulf Coast Eagles]] and the [[Little Rock Trojans men's basketball|Little Rock Trojans]]. ==Early life and high school== Tucker grew up in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]] and attended [[Northside Christian Academy]]. As a senior, he averaged 24 points, 10 rebounds, 5 assists, 3 steals and 3 blocks per game and helped lead Knights to the state championship game.{{cite web|url=https://www.naplesnews.com/story/sports/blogs/eye-on-eagles/2016/01/06/eagles-tucker-starting-to-take-flight/86077290/|title=Eagles' Tucker starting to take flight|first=Dana|last=Caldwell|work=[[Naples Daily News]]|date=January 6, 2016|accessdate=December 21, 2019}} Tucker committed to play college basketball at Florida Gulf Coast over offers from [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]], [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]], [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]], and [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]].{{cite web|url=http://nestbackup.blogspot.com/2014/09/2015-sf-rayjon-tucker-commits-to-fgcu.html|title=2015 SF Rayjon Tucker Commits To FGCU|website=NestBackUp.Blogspot.com/|accessdate=December 21, 2019}} ==College career== Tucker began his collegiate career with the [[Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball|Florida Gulf Coast Eagles]]. As a freshman, he averaged 6.2 points and 3.1 rebounds per game in 35 games played, starting one. Tucker averaged 7.7 points and 2.9 rebounds in 18.8 minutes per game as a sophomore.{{cite web|url=https://www.naplesnews.com/story/sports/college/fgcu/2017/06/19/rayjon-tuckers-loss-makes-three-transferring-fgcu-whats-up/408792001/|title=Tucker's loss makes three transferring from FGCU|first=Dana|last=Caldwell|work=[[Naples Daily News]]|date=June 19, 2017|access-date=December 20, 2019}} He announced his intention to transfer from the school at the end of the season.{{cite web|url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2017/06/17/high-flying-guard-rayjon-tucker-to-transfer-from-florida-gulf-coast/|title=High-flying guard Rayjon Tucker to transfer from Florida Gulf Coast|first=Scott|last=Phillips|website=[[NBCSports.com]]|date=June 17, 2017|access-date=December 20, 2019}} Tucker transferred to the University of Arkansas-Little Rock. After sitting out a season due to NCAA transfer rules, he averaged 20.3 points and 6.7 rebounds per game and was named second team All-[[Sun Belt Conference]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26309371/little-rock-tucker-coveted-transfer|title=Little Rock's Tucker to be coveted as transfer|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=March 19, 2019|access-date=December 20, 2019}} Following the season, Tucker left the program with the intention of joining a higher-level program as a graduate transfer while also declaring for the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/kansas/Article/Report-Rayjon-Tucker-to-choose-between-KU-Memphis-Iowa-State-Auburn-West-Virginia-131800466/|title=Report: Rayjon Tucker zeroing in on transfer decision|first=Scott|last=Chasen|work=247Sports.com|date=May 5, 2019|access-date=December 20, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Rayjon-Tucker-NBA-Draft-Little-Rock-Auburn-North-Carolina-West-Virginia-Graduate-Transfer-Mempis-131233187/|title=Rayjon Tucker declares for Draft, sets visits to Auburn, Memphis|work=247Sports.com|first=Evan|last=Daniels|date=April 15, 2019|access-date=December 20, 2019}} He committed to transfer to [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] over offers from [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]].{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/2019/05/12/memphis-rayjon-tucker-commits-nba-draft|title=Top Grad Transfer Rayjon Tucker Commits to Memphis, Leaves Name in NBA Draft|first=Jenna|last=West|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=May 12, 2019|accessdate=December 21, 2019}} However, Tucker ultimately decided not to pull out of the Draft and to pursue professional basketball instead.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/rayjon-tucker-stay-nba-draft-002540791.html|title=Rayjon Tucker to stay in NBA draft weeks after committing to Memphis|first=Travis|last=Hines|website=[[Yahoo Sports]]|accessdate=December 12, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Wisconsin Herd (2019)=== [[File:Rayjon Tucker.jpg|thumb|right|Tucker with the [[Wisconsin Herd]] in 2019]] After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Tucker played for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] NBA Summer League team.{{cite web|first=David|last=Cobb|title=Former Memphis Tigers commit Rayjon Tucker not looking back as NBA summer league begins|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/nba/grizzlies/2019/07/05/former-memphis-basketball-commit-rayjon-tucker-not-looking-back/1615087001/|work=[[The Commercial Appeal]]|date=July 5, 2019|access-date=December 20, 2019}} After averaging 10.2 points and 3.6 rebounds in five summer league games, the Bucks signed Tucker to an Exhibit 10 contract on August 16, 2019.{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Velazquez|title=The Milwaukee Bucks add Rayjon Tucker, Jaylen Adams to fill training-camp roster|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2019/08/16/milwaukee-bucks-sign-jaylen-adams-training-camp-contract/2035207001/|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=August 16, 2019|access-date=December 20, 2019}} Tucker was waived by the Bucks on October 19, 2019, and was subsequently assigned to their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Bucks Waive Tucker, Lacey, Jones|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2019/10/bucks-waive-tucker-lacey-jones.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 19, 2019|access-date=December 20, 2019}} He was considered an excellent teammate who once grabbed water for the players in a game he did not play in.{{cite news|first=Rushin|last=Jerell|title=Rayjon Tucker was the ideal teammate with the Wisconsin Herd before getting NBA contract|url=https://www.thenorthwestern.com/story/sports/2020/01/23/wisconsin-herd-excited-former-player-rayjon-tucker-earning-nba-contract-utah-jazz/4527993002/|work=[[Oshkosh Northwestern]]|date=January 23, 2020|access-date=February 11, 2020}} Tucker averaged 23.8 points, 4.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists, and 0.9 steals per game in 33.8 minutes played in 16 games with the Herd before signing an NBA contract with the Jazz.{{cite web|first=Mychal|last=Lowman|title=Utah Jazz sign Rayjon Tucker from G-League Wisconsin 2019|access-date=December 25, 2019}} Tucker was named the G League Player of the Month for December and Midseason All-NBA G League for the Eastern Conference.{{cite 2021}} ===Return to Wisconsin / Denver Nuggets (2021–2022)=== Tucker joined the [[Wisconsin Herd]] for the [[2021–22 NBA G League season]].{{cite web|title=Wisconsin Herd Announces 2021 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/wisconsin-herd-announces-2021-training-camp-roster/n-5758540|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 26, 2021|access-date=October 31, 2021}} On December 21, 2021, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN FORWARD CHRIS SILVA AND GUARD RAYJON TUCKER TO 10-DAY CONTRACTS|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-chris-silva-and-rayjon-tucker|website=NBA.com|date=December 21, 2021|access-date=December 21, 2021}} After not playing for the Timberwolves during his stint, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Denver Nuggets]] on December 31.{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets Sign Rayjon Tucker to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-rayjon-tucker-123121|website=NBA.com|date=December 31, 2021|access-date=January 1, 2022}} He played in three games for the Nuggets.{{cite web|title=Rayjon Tucker 2021-22 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/tuckera01/gamelog/2022|website=basketball-reference.com|access-date=August 2, 2022}} He returned to the Herd on January 11, 2022.{{cite web|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 11, 2022}} On February 3, he scored 31 points and had six rebounds in a loss to the [[Lakeland Magic]].{{cite news|title=Rayjon Tucker: Thriving in G League|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rayjon-tucker-thriving-in-g-league/|website=CBSSports.com|date=February 5, 2022|access-date=February 5, 2022}} In 27 games for the Heard, he averaged 21.1 points, 7.6 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 1.3 steals per game.{{cite web|title=Rayjon Tucker 2021-22 Game Log|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/player/1629730/|website=gleague.nba.com|access-date=August 2, 2022}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2022)=== On April 8, 2022, Tucker signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|first=Parker|last=Goran|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Rayjon Tucker|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-rayjon-tucker|website=NBA.com|date=April 8,
